name: Kunze Jiang
description: Kunze Jiang is a master's student at the University of Science and Technology of China, researching multimodal reasoning, self-distillation, reinforcement learning, and efficient video generation.
bio: I am currently pursuing an M.Eng. in Computer Technology at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC, 2025–2028). I received my B.Eng. in Computer Science and Technology from Jiangxi Normal University (2021–2025).
My research interests include LLM post-training, on-policy distillation, and reinforcement learning.
My recent work explores hint-informed self-distillation for reasoning segmentation and dynamic sparse attention for efficient video diffusion transformers.

news.text: Released Hint-Informed Self-Distillation for Reasoning Segmentation (HISD).
Released Mixture of Distributions Matters: Dynamic Sparse Attention for Efficient Video Diffusion Transformers (MOD-DiT).

publications.title: Mixture of Distributions Matters: Dynamic Sparse Attention for Efficient Video Diffusion Transformers

experience.role: Research on Reasoning Segmentation · Co-first Author
description: Uses offline Segment Hints and a hint-conditioned EMA teacher for token-level credit assignment, improving target disambiguation while encouraging concise reasoning.
Requires neither hints nor a teacher at inference.

experience.role: Research on Efficient Video Generation · Co-author
description: Introduces sampling-free dynamic sparse attention for video diffusion transformers.
Predicts evolving attention patterns from early denoising steps and applies online block masking to accelerate video generation while preserving quality.
